message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season (typically late winter to early spring). A male will approach a receptive female, often after a scent-marking display. He may roar or use body language to signal interest. If the female accepts, they engage in a brief courtship ritual—sniffing each other’s genital area, licking, and vocalizing. Once the female signals readiness, copulation occurs, lasting only a few minutes. After mating, the male may guard the female from rivals, but he does not participate in raising the cubs.
